grinder_calibration.zero: Turn dial counter-clockwise to just-starting resistance; stop, do not overtighten; calibrate dial marker at #0 if needed.
grinder_calibration.display_format: R.N.C = full rotations / number (0–5) / extra clicks (0–9), clockwise from zero; e.g., 2.1.5 = 135 clicks.
grinder_calibration.grind_estimate_policy: All recipe-specific X-Ultra settings are editorial starting estimates derived from manufacturer method bands. Not published or experimentally verified by any roaster.

coffees.name: Eliane Lívio
coffees.producer: Eliane Lívio and Pedro / CAFESUL cooperative
coffees.bio: Eliane Lívio and her husband Pedro cultivate Conilon near Muqui in Espírito Santo. Their coffee is sold through CAFESUL; Eliane also helped found the Pó de Mulheres women-producer initiative. Quijote roasts this washed 2025 crop medium-dark, retaining a lively, nutty sweetness and unusually plush texture for Canephora.
coffees.recommendation: The gentler Switch approach may retain hazelnut and grape-like sweetness without amplifying roast bitterness; contrast with the brighter V60.
warnings: Roaster publishes espresso positioning, not a bean-specific V60/Switch/AeroPress recipe.
Exact farm altitude was not specified in the checked product listing.

steps: 0:00 wet grounds with 45 g of water; allow ~35–40 seconds of bloom.
0:40 pour gently to 115 g total, keeping the bed evenly wet.
1:15 pour to 190 g total.
1:50 pour to 270 g total and allow to draw down. Avoid aggressive swirling with dark roasts.
recipes.notes: This V60 pulse schedule is an editorial suggested implementation; tune flow to the listed drawdown target.

grind_x_ultra.dial_in: Start at the listed setting. If thin/underdeveloped and draining too fast, go ~4 clicks finer. If drying/bitter, or draining too slowly, go ~4 clicks coarser; cool water 1–2°C for harsh dark roasts. Taste takes priority over the clock.
grind_x_ultra.basis: Estimated from the X-Ultra manufacturer pour-over zone, this recipe’s intended flow, and the bean’s roasting/processing. Not cup-tested.

steps: Rinse V60/Switch paper, place on server and close the Switch valve.
Add 20 g of coffee and 300 g of water at 89°C, fully saturating all grounds.
Give one gentle stir/swirl to remove dry pockets; leave closed for 3:00.
Open the valve and allow the brew to pass through the paper. Taste both warm and cooler.
recipes.notes: Editorial experiment targeting body and sweetness. Full-dose recipe assumes Switch **03 (~360 mL)**. On Switch **02 (~200 mL)** use **12 g coffee / 180 g water**, same temperature and steep; the smaller cup will differ slightly in ratio. Do not overfill beyond the brewer’s rated capacity. Steep time precedes drawdown.

grind_x_ultra.dial_in: If flat/weak, go ~5 clicks finer or steep 30 seconds longer. If muddy/drying or painfully slow to drain, go ~5 coarser or steep shorter. Clocked steep ends when valve opens, not when drawdown finishes.
grind_x_ultra.basis: Estimated from broad X-Ultra pour-over and coarse-brewing zones, adjusted for a closed-valve steep; maker provides no dedicated Switch calibration.

steps: Use standard AeroPress orientation, a rinsed paper filter, and a stable heat-safe mug.
Add 15 g of ground coffee. At 0:00, add 225 g of water at 89°C and stir gently 2–3 times.
Insert the plunger just far enough to form a seal; do not press yet.
Begin a slow, controlled press after roughly 1:45–1:50 total elapsed time; finish around ~2:15.
recipes.notes: Editorial AeroPress starting point, not a bean-specific roaster recipe. Fits a standard AeroPress chamber; a capped, gentle steep reduces dripping. Do not try to fit Seekind’s published 300 g pour-over dose in a standard AeroPress chamber.

grind_x_ultra.dial_in: If weak/underdeveloped, go ~4 clicks finer or extend immersion slightly. If pressing is difficult or the cup is harsh, go ~4 clicks coarser, lower temperature slightly, or press more gently.
grind_x_ultra.basis: Estimated from the X-Ultra manufacturer AeroPress zone and the recommended steep/press recipe. Not cup-tested.

coffees.name: Microconda
coffees.bio: A limited 2025 Ecuadorian lot from WAYLLA KURI: the producers retained some fruit mucilage during drying, yielding a honey-processed Robusta. Quijote describes greater creaminess, body and sweetness compared with its standard washed Cremaconda.
coffees.recommendation: A short, cooler Switch steep may emphasize cane-sugar sweetness without making the dark roast too dominant. Use a small sample before committing a whole bag to filter brewing.
warnings: This is an espresso roast; all three filter/immersion methods are editorial experiments.
Availability on Quijote listing may vary by weekly batch and pack size.

coffees.name: Cremaconda
coffees.producer: WAYLLA KURI cooperative (historical relationship also includes JATARY)
coffees.bio: A washed 2025 crop from WAYLLA KURI, produced by indigenous families in mixed forest-garden chakras in Ecuador’s Amazonian lowlands. Quijote emphasizes dark chocolate, liquorice, strong body, dense crema and a surprisingly soft texture.
coffees.recommendation: Try a cool, concentrated AeroPress cup before a V60: paper filtration may isolate the vanilla/chocolate notes while reducing heavy crema-like body.
warnings: Quijote explicitly markets this as dark espresso; V60, Switch and AeroPress recipes are editorial only.
Availability may change with weekly allocations.

coffees.name: Gio 100% Canephora (Omniroast)
coffees.farm: Kichwa community smallholders in the Sumaco Biosphere Reserve
coffees.bio: Produced with Kichwa communities in Ecuador’s Sumaco Biosphere Reserve and marketed through Giomar Hidalgo’s Latitud 0° project. This Napo Payamino yellow-honey Canephora is intentionally roasted for both espresso and paper-filter brewing. Seekind lists 900 m elevation and a coffee-specific five-pour recipe.
coffees.recommendation: Use the manufacturer-listed V60 recipe as your control cup, then give it a 3:30 Switch immersion to see whether the cocoa-nib body grows without sacrificing clarity.
warnings: Seekind also says its 20 g / 300 g filter recipe is suitable for AeroPress, but five 60 g pours and 300 g water are not reproduced as an AeroPress procedure; the AeroPress method here is editorial.

steps: 0:00 add 60 g water and bloom for 30 seconds.
0:30 add 60 g (120 g total).
1:00 add 60 g (180 g total).
1:30 add 60 g (240 g total).
2:00 add final 60 g (300 g total), then allow to finish by about 2:30–3:00.
recipes.notes: Published coffee-specific filter recipe: 20 g / 300 g, 93°C, medium grind and five 60 g additions at 30-second intervals. Carried over unchanged in essentials; V60 is the selected hand-filter implementation.

coffees.name: Vietnam RoSé
coffees.bio: A single-origin 100% Fine Robusta from Great Cherry in Đắk Lắk, made from the Ro Sé variety and processed as an anaerobic natural. The roaster describes distinct papaya and chocolate-raisin sweetness despite a strongly developed espresso roast.
coffees.recommendation: A shorter, lower-temperature V60 may expose the papaya layer; a longer closed Switch steep may instead amplify its syrupy raisin sweetness.
warnings: The roaster recommends espresso/moka first, with filter as an experiment; no bean-specific V60, Switch or AeroPress quantities were found.

coffees.name: Vietnam Siêu Sao
coffees.bio: A Gia Lai Fine Robusta treated with a 144-hour anaerobic natural process. Aroma Hoch 3 highlights pistachio, nougat and honeydew melon. The product listing describes the coffee as an espresso rather than a dedicated filter roast.
coffees.recommendation: Try a longer, gentle Switch immersion with minimal agitation as a counterpart to the conventional V60: the hypothesis is stronger pistachio-and-melon sweetness, not a guarantee.
warnings: The Siêu Sao page appears to include unrelated Guatemala Los Volcanes product-copy lower down. Origin, process and tasting details here come only from its Siêu Sao-specific opening and collection listing.
Cultivar and exact farm altitude not established.

coffees.name: Mr Toi — 100% Fine Robusta
coffees.bio: A deeply roasted Peaberry Canephora lot from Nguyen Van Toi’s Future Coffee Farm near Bảo Lộc. The roaster reports anaerobic natural processing, robust body and dense crema. Its collection tasting notes emphasize popcorn, wild honey and vanilla.
coffees.recommendation: Try a cooler, short AeroPress brew as an alternative to espresso, prioritizing creamy vanilla sweetness over heavy roast intensity.
warnings: This is NOT assumed to be the same roast/lot as Mókuska Mr. Toi or Südhang Mr Toi.
The roaster’s collection lists popcorn/wild honey/vanilla, while body copy elsewhere on its page mentions popcorn/roasted almond/date; both are descriptive, not user tastings.

coffees.region: Villa Rica, San Pedro de Pichanaz
coffees.producer: Cooperativa Agraria Cafetalera CEPRO Yanesha / Yanesha community
coffees.varietal: Five local Canephora varieties (individual names not published)
coffees.bio: An organic Fine Robusta produced by indigenous Yanesha farmers on remote, biodiverse Peruvian agroforestry plots. The cooperative CEPRO Yanesha manages and quality-controls a mixture of five long-established Canephora varieties. Laufenmühle offers distinct filter and espresso roast versions of the same coffee.
coffees.recommendation: Start with a straightforward V60 and compare a 3:30 Switch. If papaya disappears under immersion, shorten steep time or lower the water temperature slightly.
warnings: The roaster does not name the wet/dry processing method on the checked listing; the process field is intentionally blank.
Same green coffee origin as Laufenmühle El Camino Espresso, but this is a distinct roast SKU.

coffees.name: Peru El Camino — Espresso roast
coffees.region: Villa Rica, San Pedro de Pichanaz
coffees.producer: Cooperativa Agraria Cafetalera CEPRO Yanesha / Yanesha community
coffees.varietal: Five local Canephora varieties (individual names not published)
coffees.bio: The deeper espresso-roast counterpart to El Camino Coffee, grown by Yanesha smallholders in high-biodiversity agroforestry at about 1,500 m and coordinated by CEPRO Yanesha. The roaster emphasizes intense chocolate, hints of tropical fruit and abundant crema; the espresso won a 2025 German Roasters’ Guild tasting gold medal.
coffees.recommendation: Brew beside the filter-roast El Camino with the same water and brewer. This isolates the effect of roast style, although grind and extraction may need individual adjustment.
warnings: Processing method is not specified; no washed/natural classification is assumed.
